body:
WHAT
Monitor starts a long-running shell command as a background task and treats each stdout line as an event. Lines that arrive within 200ms are batched into one background_notification (kind monitor_events) plus one <task-notification> reminder that the model sees on its next turn; the running turn is not interrupted. stderr goes only to the task output file. More than 600 lines in 60s stops the monitor for noise; unless persistent, it is killed after timeout_ms.

WHY
Without it the agent would have to poll a log with repeated Bash calls, and a flood of output would spam the context.

WHERE
engine/tools/src/monitor.ts — monitorTool (permissionClass 'execute'), execute() -> ctx.session.background.launch({ kind:'monitor', start }), start(): spawnShell(command, ctx.cwd, false), line splitting on stdout, onLine() with eventTimes/NOISE_LIMIT/NOISE_WINDOW_MS, flush() emitting background_notification kind 'monitor_events' and ctx.session.remind() (BATCH_REMINDER_CAP summary), the noise stop path (kind 'monitor_stopped', background.stop), timeout kill via killTree(). Constants BATCH_WINDOW_MS 200, NOISE_LIMIT 600, DEFAULT_TIMEOUT 300000.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. With a real BackgroundManager in a temp stateDir and a recording emit/remind, run Monitor { command: 'echo a; echo b; echo c' }; assert execute() returns immediately with 'Monitor started with task id: monitor_', and after the child exits exactly one monitor_events notification with payload.lines ['a','b','c'] and one remind() containing '3 event line(s)' were produced.
2. Run Monitor { command: 'echo x; sleep 1; echo y' }; assert two separate monitor_events notifications (lines split by the 200ms batch window) and that remind() was called, not that any tool result was returned mid-turn.
3. Run Monitor { command: 'echo err 1>&2; echo out' }; assert 'err' is in the task output file and not in any monitor_events payload, while 'out' is in the payload.
4. Run Monitor { command: 'yes | head -700' } (or a loop printing 700 lines fast); assert a monitor_stopped notification with payload.reason 'noise' and background.get(id).status 'stopped'.
5. Run Monitor { command: 'sleep 5', timeout_ms: 1000 }; assert the child is killed within ~1s; run with persistent:true and assert it is still running after 1.5s until background.stop(id).
